questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions Using the Product or Quotient Rule
questions.worked_solution:
Applying the product rule, using the formula for the derivative of $arctanx$ and applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =arctan({x}^{3})\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1))+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arctan({x}^{3})) \\  & =arctan({x}^{3})\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+1)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)\cdot \frac{1}{1+({x}^{3})^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}) \\  & =arctan({x}^{3})\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\cdot 2x+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)\cdot \frac{1}{1+({x}^{3})^{2}}\cdot 3{x}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2xarctan({x}^{3})}{{x}^{2}+1}+\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)}{1+{x}^{6}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the slope of the tangent line to the curve $f(x)=6\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{x}^{2}-2x)$ at $x=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arctangent is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[6\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3{x}^{2}-2x)] \\  & =6\cdot \frac{1}{1+(3{x}^{2}-2x)^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{2}-2x) \\  & =\frac{6}{1+9{x}^{4}-12{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}}\cdot (6x-2) \\  & =\frac{36x-12}{9{x}^{4}-12{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line to the curve $y=f(x)$ at $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(1) & =\frac{36(1)-12}{9({1}^{4})-12({1}^{3})+4({1}^{2})+1} \\  & =\frac{24}{2} \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions Using the Product or Quotient Rule
questions.worked_solution:
Applying the product rule, using the formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arccos}⁡x$ and applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{arccos}⁡(5-x)) & =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(5-x)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡(5-x)) \\  & =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(5-x)\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{(5-x)}^{2}}})\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5-x) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{arccos}⁡(5-x)-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\sqrt{1-{(5-x)}^{2}}}\cdot (-1) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\sqrt{1-{(5-x)}^{2}}}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{arccos}⁡(5-x).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arctangent is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(7{x}^{4})] \\  & =\frac{1}{1+{(7{x}^{4})}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7{x}^{4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+49{x}^{8}}\cdot 28{x}^{3} \\  & =\frac{28{x}^{3}}{49{x}^{8}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arccosine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[2\operatorname{arccos}⁡(1+x)] \\  & =2(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(1+x)^{2}}})\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1+x) \\  & =-\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-(1+2x+{x}^{2})}} \\  & =-\frac{2}{\sqrt{-2x-{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent line to the curve at $x=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-1} \\  & =-\frac{2}{\sqrt{-2(-1)-(-1)^{2}}} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$
